I need to find residues that make contact with both P143 and T151, so I'm pulling out their atomic coordinates to check spatial proximity to nearby residues.

These two residues are quite far apart spatially, roughly 11.8 Å between their CA atoms, so any bridging residue needs a long side chain reaching between them. I'm checking K147's lysine side chain distances to P143 atoms, but the closest measurement (NZ to CB) comes out to about 4.29 Å, just over a typical contact cutoff, so it's not quite there—now I'm moving on to check R148's coordinates instead.

I'm working through R148's arginine side chain geometry, but its CA-CA distance to T151 looks too far to be a contact. So now I'm checking whether K147 might instead be interacting with T151, comparing K147's backbone carbonyl position against T151's nitrogen coordinate.

That distance comes out around 2.94 Å, confirming a contact. This fits the i,i+4 pattern typical of a helix, so I'm now examining whether the same spacing holds between P143 and K147 across this stretch of residues, and their oxygen-to-nitrogen distance also comes out around 2.84 Å, confirming that contact too.

Since the question expects only one answer, I check other candidates like V149 and R148 against P143, but their distances look too far apart in the helix to qualify. So the answer is K147.
